params.body:
## What

The error pages (403, 404, 419, 429, 500 and the 503 maintenance page) were Dutch for every visitor, with `<html lang="nl">`. A French dealer who mistyped an address, or the visitor of a dealer's German site during maintenance, read Dutch.

- Every text of those pages (title, explanation, the "back to the dashboard" button, the maintenance page's heading, contact line, refresh note and the embed variant) now lives in a new group `resources/lang/{nl,fr,en,de}/errors.php`. The Dutch wording is unchanged.
- `<html lang>` follows the chosen language on both layouts.
- The maintenance page's contact sentence is escaped and the mail address is put back in as a link, so the translations carry no HTML.

## Locale resolution

One place: `App\Support\ErrorLocale::for($request)`, called from `Handler::renderHttpException` (the path every HTTP error page takes, including 419 from a token mismatch, 500 in production and 503 from maintenance mode). The locale is set for the rendering only and restored afterwards.

1. When the session is running (the error was thrown inside the `web` group): what the app itself chose, via `SetLangMiddleware::chosen()`, the same order the middleware uses: language switch in the session, the signed-in user's language, `?lang=`, the website's session language, the legacy numeric session value.
2. The browser's `Accept-Language`, matched against nl, fr, en and de with the region ignored (`fr-BE` is French; the first supported language in the header wins).
3. The app default, nl.

There is no locale cookie in between: the platform keeps the choice in the session and sets no cookie for it. So a 404 on an address no route matches, and the maintenance page, come before the session and follow the browser, also for a signed-in dealer. A 403 or an `abort(404)` inside a screen follows the user.

`SetLangMiddleware` got its order extracted into `chosen()` and a `SUPPORTED` constant; `handle()` does exactly what it did before.

Spanish is not offered here: `SetLangMiddleware` does not pick it and `LanguageParityTest` only reports its gaps, so `errors.php` exists for the four enforced languages.

## Tests

- `ErrorPagesSpeakTheVisitorsLanguageTest` (13 tests): 404 with `fr-BE,fr;q=0.9` is French with `lang="fr"`; `de` is German; `es` falls back to Dutch; no header is Dutch; the first supported language in a mixed header wins; a signed-in French user gets French on a 403 and on an `abort(404)` inside the web group whatever the browser says; the session language switch wins; an unmatched address with a signed-in French user follows the browser (documents the missing session there); the locale is restored after rendering; every errors view renders in nl, fr, en and de without a raw `errors.*` key; every key is translated and not left Dutch; the mail link survives on the maintenance page in every language.
- `MaintenanceModeTest`: sends a Dutch `Accept-Language` in `setUp` (the test client sends `en-us` by default) and gains a French maintenance page test.
- Removing the call in the handler fails 5 of the new tests.
- Full suite locally: 2483 tests, OK (1 skipped, 1 incomplete: the existing Spanish gap report). PHPStan: no errors. Pint on the new files.

## Business rules

New rule R P2-2.17 in `32-p2-mijn-garage.md` (error pages in the reader's language, the resolution order, and that an unknown address and the maintenance page follow the browser). Tagged `@rule P2-2.17` in the tests.

Note: a maintenance page prerendered with `php artisan down --render=...` is rendered once on the command line and stays Dutch; the default `down` renders per request and follows the browser.
params.title: Error pages speak the visitor's language
